localChanges: After loading a saved game, ships could no longer take units aboard or put them ashore, and a computer player that owned a ship stopped taking its turns. Ships, and the computer players who own them, now work after a load, including in games saved before this fix (closes #228).
A computer player's ship carrying a unit onto a tile that an enemy city was working no longer makes that ship lose its turn (#225).

log: `civ1-city:unit/moved/release-occupied-worked-tile` read the tile's `WorkedTile` in its criteria and again in its effect, assuming nothing changed in between. `RuleRegistry#process` checks every rule's criteria before running any effect, and `civ1-unit:unit/moved/move-cargo` (an earlier effect) moves the transport's cargo onto the same tile. Each cargo unit's own `Moved` rules release the tile, so by the time this rule's effect ran for the transport, `getByTile` returned null and `workedTile.city()` threw a TypeError (civ-clone/web-renderer#225: a Trireme carrying a Catapult, seed 15 at 300 turns).

The two views of "worked" never disagreed: the effect acted on a stale answer. The rule now looks the tile up once more in its effect, with the same test as the criterion (another player's city works it, not as its centre), and does nothing when an earlier effect has released it.
The test moves a real Trireme with a Warrior aboard through civ1-unit's `Moved` rules, registered ahead of this package's as in a game.
chore: CI compiles and fails on stale compiled output, as core-strategy's does (civ-clone/web-renderer#66)

`Rules/City/{captured,created,grow,shrink,tile-reassigned}.ts` import core-player-world, and `Rules/City/cost.ts` the three base-city-yield-*-support packages, but those were dev dependencies, so a consumer only had them through other packages. They're dependencies now. civ1-unit and civ1-world were listed in both; simple-world-generator was used by nothing (civ-clone/web-renderer#66).

`Game.inject` gives `_transportRegistry` the game's `transports` and `_transportRuleRegistry` its `rules`, now that core-unit-transport declares both transient. Without them a ship came back from a load holding plain arrays, and `cargo()` threw (civ-clone/web-renderer#228).
core-strategy's compile step: `ts:compile -- --force`, so a fresh checkout's timestamps can't skip the compile, then fail on stale or uncommitted output.

It recorded core-city ^0.1.0 at 0.1.12 against package.json's ^0.1.16, and CI installs with --no-frozen-lockfile and rewrites it anyway, so it locked nothing. Like the other engine repos, CI now tests what a consumer resolves.

core-strategy 0.1.6 accepts the generator but stores nothing, because ties are ordered by registration rather than by a draw. The stale pnpm-lock.yaml held core-strategy at an older version, which hid this; without the lock file, CI resolves what a consumer gets.

`_transportRegistry` and `_transportRuleRegistry` were saved as state: each ship carried a dump of every rule, and came back from a load holding plain arrays where the registries should be, so `cargo()`, `hasCargo()`, `stow()` and `unload()` threw (civ-clone/web-renderer#228). Both are now declared `transient` on the mixin, and `Game.inject` supplies them.

`Transport(Base)` now returns a named type, `TransportClass` (`typeof Unit & TransportMixin`, whose instances are `Unit & ITransportUnit`), instead of an inferred class expression. The inferred type could not be written to the `.d.ts` (TS4094 for `Unit`'s private members, TS2742 for types reached through other packages), so the package did not compile and the committed `.js` and `.d.ts` were stale (civ-clone/web-renderer#20). `ITransportUnit` and `TransportMixin` are exported alongside it.

The standard workflow now compiles with `--force` and fails on stale or uncommitted output, as core-strategy's does. That step could not pass while `Transport.ts` failed to compile (civ-clone/web-renderer#20).
